newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania cabinet to approve 1997 draft budget.
newsitem.headline: Romania cabinet to approve 1997 draft budget.

text.p: Romania's government said on Tuesday it would approve the 1997 draft state budget this week.

"Talks on the draft state and social insurance budgets are still under way and they will be approved on Saturday in another government meeting," government spokesman Eugen Serbanescu told a news conference.
After approval, the draft will be submitted to parliament, where the ruling centrist coalition, which ousted leftists in elections last year, has a comfortable majority.
Two weeks ago, the cabinet unveiled a 1997 draft budget under which the consolidated budget deficit was forecast lower at 4.5 percent of gross domestic product, against 5.8 in 1996.
Serbanescu also said the government would work out or ammend around 50 laws and decrees by end-April to underpin the implementation of the reform programme.

The budget deficit figure was agreed during talks with the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank last month. Both lenders suspended loans for Romania in 1996 over foreign exchange curbs and overspending by the former ruling leftists in an election year.
Romania hopes to get around $1.0 billion in total loans from the IMF and World Bank to back up market reforms.
The consolidated budget includes state budget, local government budgets, social security expenditure, supplementary pension funds and various other extra-budgetary funds.

Year-on-year inflation is forecasted at 89.5 percent against 56.9 percent in 1996, after liberalisation of fuel, electricity and food prices. Romania expects a 2.0 percent GDP fall in 1997 after 4.1 percent growth last year. ($=7,744 lei)
